**Charter-global defects, demonstrated against this world.**

- **F1 (undeclared override of base `tradein_quote_acceptance` S5) hands the root problem a second answer.** `business_asset_list_required: True` for Renew Bulk IT Refresh Agreement and the entry gate requires `asset_list_filed: True`, so base's "the units on the list govern what may be collected" is in force and is superseded nowhere in `tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units.overwrite` (which names the linked-purchase clause instead). The units on the schedule are `device_count = 46`, and the customer states the same ("forty six are on the schedule and the crates will hold them all"). So base yields `units_declared = **46**` where the extended rule yields `units_declared = **5**` (recomputed below). Two defensible figures for the scored parameter, both grounded in the merged charter.
- **F6 (base `tradein_data_sanitisation`) makes the middle write of the tree contradictory.** Six `tradein_data_wipe_certify` rows stand against 18 devices booked in, and base says "a business agreement is not closed out until every serial on the asset list carries one" (`wipe_certificate_issued: True`). `credit_batch_settlement_af2cb6f5` sets `status="credited"`, i.e. closes the agreement out, with 12 serials uncertified. Under base the correct action today is not to credit; under `tradein_ext_batch_settlement_credit` it is to credit 3819.43 with a 300.00 holdback. Act-now versus cannot-act, on the same records, with no `overwrite` anywhere naming the base sentence — and this difficulty exposes no tool that records an erasure certificate, so an agent that follows base has no way forward except a handoff.
- **F2 (base `tradein_credit_issue_rules` S5) bites on this world.** `tradein_events.f0a63899…` is already a `tradein_credit_issue` row of 900.00 on `bf9b906b…` (2026-09-16), and `credit_outstanding` is 900.0. Base: "the credit is issued once for the batch rather than device by device". The extended write books a second `tradein_credit_issue` row on the same batch. A reader who takes base at its word concludes the batch has had its credit; a reader who follows the extended rule nets the 900.00 off and credits the difference.
- **F3 (base `tradein_device_logistics` S6) gives the revised offer a second answer.** 18 devices were booked in against a request for 21, and base settles that case: "A shipment arriving with fewer units than the request declared is booked in at the units actually received, and the agreement is appraised on those" — i.e. `appraised_amount` already covers only the 18. `tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount` multiplies by `booked_share = 18/21` again. Without the second proration the figure is `RND(5700.00 × 0.88, 2) = **5016.00**`; with it, **4299.43**. `tradein_device_logistics` is in neither this policy's `base_policy_refs` nor any `overwrite`.
- **F8 (seed against base grading) gives a third reading of the same figure.** Base `tradein_appraisal_grading`: "The amount the appraisal supports is the quoted amount times the percentage the programme's condition ladder gives for the condition found, rounded to the cent." For Renew Business Asset Buyback the ladder gives `fair: 70`, so the amount the appraisal supports for `appraised_condition: fair` on `quoted_amount: 6300.0` is `4410.00`, not the seeded `appraised_amount: 5100.0` (no grade on the ladder — 100/90/70/40/20/0 — yields 5100.00 from 6300.00). A reader who computes the supported amount as base directs gets `gap = 1890.00 > 2 × 630.00` → third tier → `offer_before_share = 4410.00` → `RND(4410.00 × 18/21 × 0.88, 2) = **3326.40**`. The extended rule's phrase "as recorded on the agreement" is the only thing excluding it, and the world it describes is one base grading cannot produce.
- **F10 costs `tradein_ext_batch_settlement_credit` its only `method` factor.** Tiers 2 and 3 of `settled_figure_basis` are the same sentence; on this world tier 1 is taken, so the duplication changes no number here, but the policy is left with a three-`when` ladder over two outcomes and, if the factor is struck, with zero `method` factors.
- **F13 costs the root computation its baseline.** `tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units.baseline.rule` names the transit-cover cap and the three holdbacks and defines none of them, so a solver who reads only that computation document cannot reach a definite number at all; the fall-back **46** that the factor baselines imply is not derivable from the baseline text, and `baseline.params` names `recent_purchase_days` and `finance_hold_balance_usd`, which that text does not use.

### problem_chain

**Root problem.** The customer asks how many machines can go in the first wave and consents to releasing them: "he wants the first wave collected on the first of October … releasing the machines is the school's decision and he will confirm that part himself". That is `tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units` (subject `tradein_quote_accept`, `computes: units_declared`, `target_tool: confirm_refresh_wave_units_923c3678`, owner=user) on agreement `56ac493d…`.

**Prerequisite sentence the root rule carries.** One: "The machines a wave of the refresh schedule carries are settled only after every batch already appraised on the profile stands credited with the amount owed on it." State form; what it waits on is `tradein_agreements.status = credited` with an amount on it, for every batch on the profile that stands appraised.

**False at the opening?** Yes. `tradein_agreements.bf9b906b-a7a5-4cd4-89ce-82d223b09586` stands `status: "appraised"` with `final_credit_amount: ""` and `credited_date: ""`. The gate is unmet. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about (`credit_batch_settlement_af2cb6f5`, which sets `status="credited"` and `final_credit_amount`), so the hop resolves in one reading.

**Second hop.** `tradein_ext_batch_settlement_credit`'s own rule carries "The amount credited is worked out only after the revised offer the appraisal calls for stands on the agreement's trade-in history." False at the opening: no `tradein_events` row on `bf9b906b…` has `event_type: "tradein_quote_revise"` (the seven rows are six `tradein_data_wipe_certify` and one `tradein_credit_issue`). Exactly one write puts a revised offer on the history (`put_revised_offer_f86761c2`), and `tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount`'s own rule says a revised offer is owed where the appraisal finds the batch other than the condition declared — which the records show (`declared_condition: good`, `appraised_condition: fair`). One reading.

**Third hop.** `tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount.prerequisite` is `[]`, and its inputs are all on record at the opening. The tree closes.

**Tree derived from the policy and the world alone:**

```
tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units            (root, owner=user, units_declared on 56ac493d…)
  └─ state_gate  ─────────────────────▶ tradein_ext_batch_settlement_credit   (final_credit_amount on bf9b906b…)
                                           └─ value_input ────────────────▶ tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount  (revised_amount on bf9b906b…)
```
n = 2 prerequisite problems, 1 `value_input` edge against a floor of max(n−1,1) = 1 ✓, no cycle, isomorphic to the declared `prerequisite` graph in nodes, edges and kinds.

**Per-edge load-bearing run.**
- `batch_settlement_credit → revised_offer_amount`: skip the revision and replay the credit — `revisions_put = 0`, `settled_amount = 5100.00`, `final_credit_amount = **4620.00**` instead of **3819.43**. The edge bears weight on a scored value.
- `refresh_wave_units → batch_settlement_credit`: skipping the credit leaves the wave's scored figure at 5 (nothing in `refresh_wave_units.compute` reads `bf9b906b…`), which is correct for a `state_gate`: what the edge carries is the eligibility, which is unmet at the opening (`status: appraised`, `final_credit_amount: ""`) and which only that write makes hold, and the terminal state differs (the older batch closed out and `credit_outstanding` moved). It is not decorative, but it is worth recording that its declared `effect` justifies the gate by "the credit the profile has been issued in the year", a quantity no binding of the blocked policy reads (`_difficulty.md` O3).

**Parallel edges.** None; the tree is a chain, so no two orders give two terminal states.

**No-wait argument.** All three resolving actions are executable in session: the revision needs only figures on the agreement, the credit needs the revision row plus records, the wave consent needs the date the customer states. The one place base would impose a wait (the decision days on a revised offer) is closed by the customer answering in session, as quoted above.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `task_tools.py:126-136` (`put_revised_offer_f86761c2`) rounds the amount and creates one event; `task_tools.py:168-182` (`credit_batch_settlement_af2cb6f5`) updates the agreement and creates one event; `task_tools.py:213-221` (`confirm_refresh_wave_units_923c3678`) is a bare `ctx.create`. None validates a prerequisite, refuses, errors or hints.

**Customer-owned write in the tree.** Yes — the root itself is `owner="user"`, handed over passively: "When the agent unlocks the release confirmation and hands it to him he runs it, reads back the count and the date it shows, and says that is right."

**Does the customer raise only the root?** Substantially yes: the two prerequisite *problems* (a revised offer, a batch credit) are never named by him, and he is explicitly passive about them ("if the agent never mentions the older batch at all he does not raise it"). He does volunteer that the older batch went in ("He knows nothing about what has happened to the batch of older Latitudes the school sent in at the start of September beyond the fact that they went"), which is background rather than a request, and every holdback fact is given only on being asked. Recorded as an observation only.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now, on all three writes.**
- The refresh schedule's quote is live: `quote_date 2026-09-16`, `quote_validity_days 45`, `quote_expiry_date 2026-10-31`.
- The revision is due today and not out of time (3 business days from 2026-09-15).
- The credit is permitted by base `creditable_agreement_state` (`status: appraised`).
- Identity: `identity_check_required: True` on both programmes; the persona gives phone `5037740193`, card `4106`, postal `97251`, all matching `customers.59d80ff6…`, so `verify_customer_identity` passes on two.
- **Closest alternative candidate, and why it is excluded.** The older batch's `quote_expiry_date` is `2026-09-03` and the devices were booked in on `2026-09-04`, i.e. the day after the quote's last day, and the blueprint's own difficulty summary lists "honouring a quote that has already expired" as a POLICY_NOT_COVERED handoff. It is excluded by the records and the charter, not by gold: base `tradein_quote_issue`'s validity clause is an eligibility on *acceptance* (`quote_still_valid`, `applies_to: [tradein_quote_expire]`), and this agreement was accepted on `2026-08-22`, inside `quote_date + 14 days`; the agreement therefore legitimately stands `appraised`, and `tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount` fixes the standing figure as "the amount quoted, or the highest revised offer already put on the agreement where that is higher". The one-day overrun is instead what puts `offer_ageing_anchor` on its first tier.

**Objects.** Two agreements on one profile `59d80ff6-ce6f-4a67-992d-f8fba22c6164`: the older batch `bf9b906b…` (serial prefix `ORAFLEET2026A`, Renew Business Asset Buyback) for the revision and the credit, and the refresh schedule `56ac493d…` (serial prefix `ORAFLEET2026B`, Renew Bulk IT Refresh Agreement) for the wave. Correlation key `tradein_agreement_id` throughout; every aggregate the charter uses is agreement-scoped, which is what keeps the older batch's `units_declared: 21` from being confused with the schedule's `46`.

**1-F1 — SOURCE-POLICY RED / SOURCE-TASK RED: base `tradein_quote_acceptance`'s asset-list sentence still governs the wave, and gives 46 where gold gives 5.**
- symptom: two defensible values for the scored `units_declared`.

(`tradein_ext_collection_handover_units`, the other units policy, declares exactly that sentence; this one does not.)
- evidence: base "A business agreement is accepted only once the signed asset list the programme requires is on file, and **the units on the list govern what may be collected**"; programme `business_asset_list_required: True`, entry gate `asset_list_filed: True`; extended `replaced_by` "The machines a wave carries are the machines the schedule covers, capped at the machines the programme's transit cover will bear, less …"; `initial_state.tradein_agreements.56ac493d….device_count = 46`; `initial_state.tradein_shipping_requests.6d92ab22….units_declared = 46` with `customer_consent: consented_by_customer` for `2026-10-01`; the customer "says forty six are on the schedule and the crates will hold them all". The task's own `design_rationale` reads the asset list as satisfied — "asset list is on file (the schedule stands quoted with its 46 machines listed)" — and then declares a different sentence superseded.
- demonstrated consequence: base's reading gives `units_declared = 46`, the extended reading gives 5 (both recomputed). A consented request for 46 machines on the requested day already stands on the schedule, so the base reading is not merely textual — it is already on the record the agent reads.
- affected artifact: `tasks/trade_in_appraisal_desk/tradein.extended.yaml:2490-2499` (`tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units.overwrite`); scored step 15.
- relation to previous revisions: first audit of this difficulty.

**1-O1 — observation: `settlement_method` is fixed by a persona line whose stated trigger is the write itself.** The parameter is one of two base-allowed forms ("invoice credit or bank transfer only"), narrowed by no policy. The persona's line is conditional on the credit already being booked — "If the agent then says the money has been credited, he asks for it against the academy's invoice account rather than a transfer" — while the fallback "does not mention it at all unless the agent raises it" is what makes it elicitable before the write. `prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint` reads it the second way ("he names the invoice account only after the agent raises the credit"), and `argument_uniqueness_tracing` cites the line without noticing the ordering.

**1-O2 — observation: the `state_gate` edge's declared `effect` names a mechanism that does not exist.** "because the credit the profile has been issued in the year is then complete" — no binding of `tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units.compute` reads the credit issued in the year, and `trade_in_value_cap_per_year_usd = 400000.0` is nowhere near engaged (900.00 + 3819.43). **1-O3 — observation: base `tradein_revision_and_decline` puts the revised offer before the data is destroyed, and six machines were wiped first.** "A device already recycled or destroyed under the programme's sanitisation rules cannot be sent back, so on those programmes the revised offer is put before the data is destroyed" — the certificates are dated 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-17, the revised offer is put on 2026-09-18. **1-O5 — observation: both `owner=user` tools are unlockable here.** `erlbench/loader.py:21` merges every difficulty's tools into one registry, and `confirm_handover_units_5801b6db` would write a byte-identical row; the discriminator is only "a Renew trade-in agreement for a palletised freight collection" against "the next wave of a Renew refresh schedule", and this world holds a Renew Business Asset Buyback agreement as well. Relatedly, `tradein_ext_collection_freight_charge` ("A palletised collection on a business buyback is charged to the profile when the run is booked", `trigger: on_request`) is not textually excluded from a Bulk IT Refresh wave, whose own `freight_fee_usd` is 245.0 — an agent could read a collection charge as due here, which `evaluation_criteria` does not contain. See `_difficulty.md` F9.

### re_derivation (the figures that moved)

Two of this task's three figures moved because the text under them changed, so revision 1's numbers are now evidence about the old charter only. I re-derived all three from the amended charter and the amended world **before** reading `computations`, by evaluating the charter's own expressions on worlds I built from `initial_state`:

- **`revised_amount` = 4822.40.** `appraisal_amount 5100.00` (now fixed by a declared override as "the figure the appraisal recorded on the agreement"), `standing_offer 6300.00`, `gap 1200.00`, `tolerance 630.00` → second tier → `offer_before_deduction 5700.00`; `cover_not_travelling 1` because `protection_plans.d501f048….transferable_flag` is now **false** and the plan stands active, `cover_days_left = DAYS(2026-09-15, 2028-02-09) = 512 > 0` → `cover_deduction 220.00`; `quote_to_receipt_days 15 > 14` → `ageing_days = DAYS(2026-08-20, 2026-09-18) = 29`; `certificates_on_record 6 > 0` and `29 > 21` → `ageing_markdown_pct 12`; and the new ordering paragraph fixes the grouping — `RND((5700.00 − 220.00) × 0.88, 2) = 4822.40`.
- **`final_credit_amount` = 4342.40.** `revisions_put 1` → `settled_amount = 4822.40`; `interim_credit_offset 900.00`; `devices_short 3`, `value_each_device 300.00` → `transit_settlement 900.00`; `appraisal_days_taken 11` → `late_allowance 60.00`; `premium_holdback 240.00`; `uncertified_devices 12`, wipe pending → `erasure_holdback 300.00`; `4822.40 − 900 + 900 + 60 − 240 − 300 = 4342.40`.
- **`credit_expiry_date` = 2026-12-17** (a new scored argument): the rule now says the expiry day "falls the programme's credit validity days after the day of issue", and `credit_validity_days = 90` on Renew Business Asset Buyback, so 2026-09-18 + 90 days.
- **`units_declared` = 5**, unchanged (`cover_units 12`, holdbacks 3 / 2 / 2).

All four match the revealed GT exactly, as do the three whole baselines (5100.00 / 5100.00 / 46) and all fourteen factor baselines (4294.40 / 5016.00 / 5480.00 / 5480.00; 4620.00 / 5242.40 / 3442.40 / 4282.40 / 4582.40 / 4642.40; 39 / 8 / 7 / 7).

### item verdicts

**1-F1 (undeclared override of the asset-list sentence) — CLOSED on both halves.** `tradein_ext_refresh_wave_units.overwrite` now names "the units on the list govern what may be collected", which is verbatim in base `tradein_quote_acceptance` and is in force on a programme with `business_asset_list_required: True`; base's other half (the asset list must be on file) is left inherited. And the record no longer asserts the rival either: `tradein_shipping_requests.6d92ab22….units_declared` is now **0** instead of 46, so the figure the base clause would have pointed at is not standing on the schedule as consented. 46 survives only as the whole-baseline fall-back, which is what it should be.

**1-F2 (base `tradein_data_sanitisation` forbidding the close-out) — CLOSED.** `tradein_data_sanitisation` is now in `base_policy_refs`, and its clause "a business agreement is not closed out until every serial on the asset list carries one" is declared superseded by "A batch is closed out before every serial on it carries its erasure certificate, and the holdback the serials without one attract stands against the credit until they do", which appears verbatim as the rule's second sentence. ### the business-days declaration, and a miss of my own

The other change landing here is the one I should have caught. Base `tradein_appraisal_grading` says the programme's appraisal days are "counted in business days from the day the device was booked in"; both `tradein_ext_revised_offer_amount` and `tradein_ext_batch_settlement_credit` compare a calendar `DAYS(...)` count against that same `P('appraisal_days')`, and until this round no `overwrite` declared the difference.

**It was materially load-bearing on this task.** The batch was booked in on Friday 2026-09-04 and appraised on Tuesday 2026-09-15. That is 11 calendar days, but exactly **7 business days** (Mon 07, Tue 08, Wed 09, Thu 10, Fri 11, Mon 14, Tue 15), and the programme's `appraisal_days` is **7**. So base's convention gives "the appraisal was recorded within the programme's appraisal days" — the fall-through, no allowance — while the extended policy's calendar count gives "more than the appraisal days and no more than twice them" — the delayed allowance of 60.00. Two defensible credits: **4282.40** under base's convention against **4342.40** under the extended one. My revision-1 check-1 sweep went sentence by sentence through that base policy and did not carry its counting convention into the two extended policies that read the figure; revisions 2 to 4 inherited the gap.

The fix is sound. The superseded fragment is verbatim in base, the clause is genuinely in force, both replacements ("…and the programme's appraisal days are read against that calendar count") are verbatim in their own rules and true to what each policy computes, and the two are compatible with each other. Adding `tradein_appraisal_grading` to this policy's `base_policy_refs` introduces no gate or precondition: that base policy's only eligibility, `appraisable_agreement_state`, applies to `tradein_appraisal_record`, while this policy's subject is `tradein_agreement_credit`. The anchor factor in the revised-offer policy is unaffected on this world — it takes its first tier, on the quote-to-receipt span of 15 days against 14 — so only the credit's allowance was ever in doubt, and it no longer is.

### re-checks

The tree is intact: both prerequisite sentences still verbatim in their amended rules, still state-form, `resolved_by` still the depended-on `target_tool`, both edges still unmet at `frozen_time` on the unchanged world, and the `value_input` edge still moving the credit from 4342.40 to 4620.00 when the revision is skipped. No added sentence duplicates, contains or is contained by either sentence (0 collisions across the whole charter). Factor structure unchanged: 4 / 6 / 4 with ≥2 `parameter` and ≥1 `method`, every ladder at three tiers or more, `baseline` equal to its own fall-through throughout.

### verdict (task 1, revision 5)

policy self-consistency **PASS** · problem tree **PASS** · factors bear weight **PASS** · unique solution **PASS**. The render-layer RED's root cause is closed at the source without repricing anything, and a conflict worth 60.00 on this task's scored credit — latent through my four earlier passes — is now declared.
